about: The short points on a number's meaning page, written by a Claude session from the course text: the course's own words, shortened, nothing added. Key = chart.position:number, or chart.position:number+partner for a center's circle. Each group is a heading and its points; sources = the knowledge/raw files the points were taken from. The full course words stay one tap away on the page. Owner's ask 2026-10-19 (test page: Allison Frank's mind center 7 with 13/4).

groups.title: In balance
points: Popular, inspiring, unconditionally loving, healing radiance, considered a wise person.
Popular because you speak from your own inner wisdom; attracts people who want to raise their own vibration.
A very spiritual and open kind of love: the 7 stands for universal love and sees everything in a reflective light.
Seeks the more profound answers in life: philosophical, idealistic and nonmaterial.
Looks beyond race or religion to the profound essence of all people: great wisdom and profoundness in your communication.
Part of your "brand": the impression people get when they first meet you, and how the public perceives you.
Popular and charismatic: people feel embraced and accepted, and quickly open up to you about their problems and concerns.
Clairvoyance and a strong intuition: success by following your intuition and being at the right place at the right time.

groups.title: Out of balance
points: Fantasy world, no grounding, tendency to lie, psychic instability.
Can seem psychologically unstable, suffering from depression or mental disorders, obvious for all to see.
Can seem manipulative: telling others about what you would like to have as if you already own it.
Above all a lack of grounding and escapism: does not act on its plans, seen as untrustworthy.
Intuitive and original in your thinking.
Strange/abnormal interests; very fascinated by strange worldviews, theories and ways of seeing the world.
May repel some people who find your way of thinking too strange or difficult to understand.
Can lead to aloofness and a quiet snobbery, silently judging others for their lack of subtlety.
Difficult to connect with other people: always looking at things from the outside, never fully joining or merging with what you observe.
